programme_name: Pre-BCR signalling and surrogate light chain expansion
functional_description: Captures the proliferative burst driven by pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) assembly and signalling at the Large Pre-B stage. VPREB1 and VPREB3 encode surrogate light chain components that pair with rearranged immunoglobulin heavy chain to form the pre-BCR, while IGLL1 (lambda5) completes the surrogate light chain heterodimer. CD79B provides the signalling subunit (Ig-beta) of the pre-BCR complex, transducing the tonic signals that trigger clonal expansion. TCL1A coactivates AKT downstream of pre-BCR signalling to promote survival and proliferation, while STMN1, UHRF1, FAM111B, and MAD2L2 reflect the consequent S-phase replication and mitotic machinery. EBF1 maintains the B-lineage transcriptional programme essential for pre-BCR gene expression.
key_evidence: VPREB1: surrogate light chain component — obligate pre-BCR structural subunit triggering Large Pre-B expansion
VPREB3: VpreB3 surrogate light chain family member — supports pre-BCR assembly and B-cell maturation
IGLL1: lambda5 surrogate light chain — heterodimerises with VpreB1 to complete pre-BCR
CD79B: Ig-beta signalling subunit — transduces pre-BCR tonic proliferative signals via ITAM phosphorylation
TCL1A: AKT coactivator — amplifies PI3K/AKT survival signalling downstream of pre-BCR
STMN1: microtubule destabiliser — marks rapid mitotic cycling during pre-BCR checkpoint expansion
MME (CD10): CALLA marker — canonical surface antigen of pre-B ALL and normal pre-B cells
suggested_validation: Conditional VPREB1 knockdown or pre-BCR blockade (anti-mu heavy chain) in primary Large Pre-B cells followed by EdU incorporation to confirm that proliferative burst is pre-BCR signalling-dependent; flow cytometry for VPREB1/CD79B co-expression to validate pre-BCR surface assembly

programme_name: ER protein processing and ERAD quality control
functional_description: Captures the ER-resident quality control machinery in plasma cells that ensures proper folding, signal peptide cleavage, and degradation of misfolded immunoglobulin chains. SEC11C cleaves signal peptides from nascent Ig chains entering the ER; SSR4 facilitates co-translational translocation; FKBP11 catalyses prolyl isomerisation for Ig folding; DERL3 and HERPUD1 are core ERAD components that retrotranslocate and ubiquitinate misfolded glycoproteins for proteasomal degradation. This is distinct from upstream translocon entry or downstream secretory transport — it centres on the ER luminal folding checkpoint and disposal of defective Ig products.
key_evidence: DERL3: derlin-family retrotranslocation channel — core ERAD component extracting misfolded Ig from ER lumen
HERPUD1: UPR-induced ubiquitin-like domain protein — recruits misfolded substrates to the ERAD complex
FKBP11: ER-resident prolyl isomerase — catalyses rate-limiting proline cis/trans isomerisation during Ig folding
SEC11C: signal peptidase complex subunit — cleaves signal peptides from translocated nascent Ig chains
SSR4: TRAP-delta translocon-associated protein — assists co-translational ER import
XBP1: UPR master regulator driving transcription of ERAD and ER chaperone genes
SELENOM: ER-resident selenoprotein with thioredoxin-like fold — contributes to oxidative protein folding and calcium regulation
suggested_validation: DERL3 or HERPUD1 knockdown in plasma cell line (e.g. MM.1S) followed by measurement of intracellular misfolded Ig accumulation via non-reducing SDS-PAGE and proteasome activity assays to confirm ERAD pathway disruption

programme_name: ER protein processing and ERAD quality control
functional_description: Captures the ER-resident protein folding, signal peptide cleavage, and misfolded protein disposal machinery in actively secreting plasma cells. SEC11C cleaves signal peptides from nascent Ig chains entering the ER; FKBP11 catalyses prolyl isomerisation critical for Ig domain folding; DERL3 and HERPUD1 are core ERAD components that retrotranslocate and ubiquitinate misfolded Ig for proteasomal degradation. SSR4 (TRAP-delta) facilitates co-translational ER import. PRDX4 maintains the oxidative ER environment required for disulfide bond formation. This programme is distinct from upstream translocon entry alone or downstream niche survival, representing the intermediate quality-control checkpoint ensuring only correctly folded IgG1/IgA1/IgK assemblies progress through the secretory pathway.
key_evidence: DERL3: derlin-family ERAD retrotranslocon component — extracts misfolded Ig from ER for proteasomal degradation
HERPUD1: UPR-induced ERAD scaffold — recruits ubiquitin ligases to misfolded substrates under ER stress
FKBP11: ER-resident prolyl isomerase — catalyses cis/trans proline isomerisation in Ig domain folding
SEC11C: signal peptidase complex subunit — cleaves signal peptides from translocated nascent Ig chains
SSR4: TRAP-delta translocon-associated protein — gates co-translational ER import of secretory proteins
PRDX4: ER-luminal peroxiredoxin — maintains oxidative environment for Ig disulfide bond formation
XBP1: UPR master TF — drives ER expansion and ERAD gene induction in plasma cells
suggested_validation: DERL3 or FKBP11 knockdown in IgG1-secreting plasma cell line (e.g., U266 or XG-1) followed by measurement of intracellular misfolded Ig accumulation (non-reducing Western blot) and secreted Ig output (ELISA) to confirm ERAD quality-control bottleneck

programme_name: ER translocon entry and ERAD quality control
functional_description: Captures the coupled processes of co-translational immunoglobulin import into the ER and ER-associated degradation (ERAD) quality control in plasma cells. SSR4 (TRAP-delta) and SEC11C (signal peptidase complex) mediate nascent Ig chain translocation and signal peptide cleavage at the ER membrane, while FKBP11 catalyses prolyl isomerisation for proper Ig folding, and DERL3 and HERPUD1 execute retrotranslocation and ubiquitin-dependent disposal of misfolded Ig chains. This is distinct from downstream UPR transcriptional programmes or BM niche survival — it captures the gatekeeping step where nascent Ig enters the ER and misfolded products are triaged for degradation.
key_evidence: SSR4: TRAP-delta translocon-associated protein — facilitates co-translational Ig import into ER lumen
SEC11C: signal peptidase complex subunit — cleaves signal peptides from nascent Ig chains after ER entry
FKBP11: prolyl isomerase — catalyses proline cis/trans isomerisation critical for Ig domain folding in ER
DERL3: derlin family ERAD retrotranslocon — extracts misfolded glycoproteins from ER for proteasomal degradation
HERPUD1: UPR-induced ERAD scaffold — recruits ubiquitin ligase complexes to misfolded ER substrates
IGHG1/IGKC: IgG1 heavy and kappa light chain constants — the secretory cargo being processed
XBP1: UPR master regulator — drives ER expansion to accommodate high-throughput Ig processing
suggested_validation: DERL3 or FKBP11 knockdown in a plasma cell line (e.g. U266 or MM.1S) followed by measurement of intracellular misfolded Ig accumulation (non-reducing western blot) and secreted Ig levels (ELISA) to confirm coupling of ERAD quality control with secretory output

programme_name: ER protein processing and ERAD quality control
functional_description: Captures the ER-resident protein folding, signal peptide cleavage, and misfolded protein disposal machinery active in immunoglobulin-secreting plasma cells. SEC11C cleaves signal peptides from nascent Ig chains entering the ER; FKBP11 catalyses prolyl isomerisation essential for Ig domain folding; PRDX4 maintains the oxidative environment for disulfide bond formation; DERL3 and HERPUD1 constitute the ERAD retrotranslocation and ubiquitin-dependent degradation pathway that eliminates misfolded Ig chains. This programme is mechanistically downstream of SEC61/SSR4-mediated ER import and distinct from the UPR transcriptional response, focusing instead on co- and post-translational quality control within the ER lumen.
key_evidence: DERL3: derlin-family ERAD retrotranslocon component — extracts misfolded Ig from ER for proteasomal degradation
HERPUD1: ER stress-induced ubiquitin-like domain protein — recruits misfolded substrates to ERAD machinery
FKBP11: ER-localised prolyl isomerase — catalyses cis/trans isomerisation of proline residues during Ig folding
SEC11C: signal peptidase complex subunit — cleaves signal peptides from translocated nascent Ig chains
PRDX4: ER-resident peroxiredoxin — maintains oxidative environment for disulfide bond formation in Ig assembly
SSR4: TRAP-delta translocon-associated subunit — facilitates co-translational ER import upstream of folding
suggested_validation: DERL3 or FKBP11 knockdown in a plasma cell line (e.g. MM.1S) followed by measurement of intracellular misfolded Ig accumulation (non-reducing SDS-PAGE) and secreted Ig titre (ELISA) to confirm ERAD and folding dependence
